# Captured regression examples

October 25 additions: `nyc-pagination`, `orlando-pagination`, `discover-la-calendar`, and `orlando-sessions` are excerpts from fresh headless-browser inspections. `validation-provenance.json` records upstream URLs, full-rendered-capture hashes and selected elements. LA retains native calendar title/date/venue attributes while excluding carousel/image markup; its two-letter performer title is intentional. Orlando retains non-event newsletter cards to verify filtering, and two explicit performances to verify append-only expansion. Fixture whitespace is normalized. The asynchronous pagination and HTTP 429 servers in the tests are synthetic regressions reproducing observed behavior; they are not publisher captures. Full captures and screenshots remain ignored operational evidence.

These small fixtures were selected from public pages/API responses inspected on October 16, 2026 (America/Chicago). They support offline parser regression checks; they do not establish current source compatibility.

- `la-calendar.html`: the first two event cards from https://www.laconventioncenter.com/events/all. The first event is AAO-HNSF, October 17–20, 2026. Missing times must remain unknown.
- `boston-calendar.html`: selected cards from https://www.boston.gov/events. Includes an internal node link, an external event link, and a repeated Digital Literacy Workshop node on different dates. Irrelevant descriptions, contact fields, and images were removed. The visible grouped dates and times are the occurrence evidence.
- `tribe-page.json`: one event from https://network.vegas/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events with `start_date=2026-10-16`, `per_page=5`, `page=1`. Its all-day flag conflicts with a timed description. Image metadata was removed. The conflict must remain visible rather than being silently corrected.

Original run captures and the initially failed Boston attempt remain in ignored `.artifacts/`. The Boston link-format tests failed before the adapter fix and passed afterward.

`jsonld-null-fields.json` is a synthetic contract fixture for optional null identifiers/countries and missing event URLs. `jsonld-url-fallback.json` is a synthetic event with a blank optional URL and a usable canonical `@id`; tests also exercise malformed URL values. Neither is a captured publisher event. Redirect/navigation-race tests use two loopback hostnames and a controlled local server; they never contact external websites.

The additional `nyc-tourism`, `orlando`, `downtown-orlando`, `san-diego`, `sf-portal`, `trade-table`, `chicago-parks`, `festivalindex`, and `dc-tourism` HTML files are bounded excerpts from the October 16/17, 2026 reconnaissance captures. Table excerpts retain a table wrapper because HTML parsing otherwise discards standalone rows. These fixtures preserve source dates and structure; they are historical parser contracts, not current event recommendations. Chicago's second card deliberately lacks a year-bearing timestamp and must be rejected rather than guessing the year. Full local captures remain in ignored artifacts.

The source-field audit adds bounded `allevents-detail`, `allevents-new-domain-detail`, `eventbrite-overnight-detail`, `discover-la-detail`, `nyc-tourism-detail`, `downtown-orlando-detail`, `boston-detail`, and `conventiongrid-card` excerpts from the October 17, 2026 rendered browser captures. Structured-data excerpts retain event identity, date/time, venue/address, postal and coordinate facts while omitting descriptions and unrelated metadata. DOM excerpts retain inspected date/occurrence/address/map elements. Boston preserves a structured/visible occurrence conflict, and the verified new AllEvents domain preserves its UTC-markup/visible-CDT conflict. The tests explicitly retain uncertainty rather than treating the conflicting claims as validated facts. Synthetic publication-page, department-metadata, title-alias and coordinate edge cases are labeled in the tests themselves.

`san-diego-calendar.html` is a November 4, 2026 excerpt of https://www.visitsandiego.com/calendar (full capture SHA-256 `3105885f68737b3d4551bd6f822dfdc25578630003d89d5747f3898e194a4f9c`): two public `.calendar .item` rows, one unlinked "Private" booking, the `Load more` control and the inline script that only unhides rows already present. The full capture had 68 rows: 58 public events and 10 private placeholders. Tests remove the script, add server pagination or relabel the private row to verify that the single-page contract fails closed.

`conventiongrid-calendar.html` is a November 5, 2026 excerpt of https://conventiongrid.com/calendar/ (full page: 1,139 cards under month headings, 1.3 MB). Cards carry "Mon D - Mon D" without a year; the year comes from the heading. Four cards (one crossing the year end) are kept and the stated total is edited to 4 so the completeness check can be exercised; tests alter the total and a card month to verify it fails closed.

`trade-table-page.html` and `tsnn-embed-page.html` are November 5, 2026 excerpts of thetradeshowcalendar.com's `index.php?vPos=100` and its `/tsnn/` embed (two rows each, displayed range and total edited to match) used to exercise the offset-table pagination contract. `tradefest-search-page.html` keeps three events of `https://tradefest.io/en/search?page=2` (query window edited to limit 3, offset 3, total 8). `conventioncalendar-venue.html` and `conventioncalendar-destinations.html` are November 5, 2026 excerpts of the Javits venue page (header, month menu, first two cards) and `/destinations` (three of twelve cards plus the rel=next pager); scripts, styles and advertising were removed.
